summary.headline: Ravindra Energy H1 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to INR 20.7 crore from INR 46.6 crore as Energy in Motion losses widened; Q2 EIM sales rose to 142 vehicles.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 total revenue of INR 190 crore and H1 revenue of INR 310 crore (vs INR 287 crore), with renewable EBITDA up to INR 53 crore in Q2 from INR 33.4 crore. Consolidated PAT after Energy in Motion (EIM) losses was INR 19 crore in Q2 (vs INR 24.4 crore) and INR 20.7 crore in H1 (vs INR 46.6 crore). EIM sold 142 electric trucks in Q2 vs 58 in Q1 and says the second half will be significantly stronger, with losses expected to narrow in Q3 and Q4. Operating renewable capacity is 261.21 MW with 231.10 MW under construction, targeting 500 MW by March 2027.

segments.name: Renewable energy (RE)
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA INR 53 crore, H1 EBITDA INR 93.7 crore; Q2 revenue split of generation INR 31 crore, trading INR 26 crore, EPC and service concession INR 133 crore. Generation was 66 million units in Q2 and 145 million units in H1.

segments.name: Energy in Motion (EIM) - electric heavy trucks
segments.commentary: Sold 142 vehicles in Q2 vs 58 in Q1; average selling price about INR 60 lakh, with 95% of sales sold without battery. Contribution margin about 6%, down from about 8%. Losses narrowed QoQ, and management targets breakeven/positive in the next financial year.

segments.name: EIM charging network
segments.commentary: Network sales INR 10.7 crore in Q2 vs INR 6.5 crore in Q1. Eight charging stations today, targeted at 15 by December 2026 and 40 by March 2027. Swaps per station utilisation below 30%.

segments.name: EIM manufacturing (Pune/Talegaon)
segments.commentary: Capacity designed at 5,000 vehicles a year, with battery plant of similar capacity. First India-assembled truck rolled out on October 30, 2026; regular production at about 200 units per month from January 2027. CATL battery pack assembly tie-up announced.

guidance_outlook: Renewable operating capacity to reach about 500 MW by March 2027, with 200-220 MW added in FY27 (about 300 MW by Q3 and about 400 MW by Q4 as stated).
FY27 renewable EPC revenue expected around INR 600 crore, with INR 200 crore booked in H1.
FY27 electricity generation revenue expected INR 141-150 crore vs INR 89 crore last year.
EIM losses expected to narrow significantly in Q3 and Q4 FY27; no numeric EIM guidance given. Second half sales to be significantly stronger than first half.
EIM network expected to reach 40 charging stations by March 2027; merger completion targeted around September 2027 (subject to SEBI and NCLT approvals).
capex_capacity: Operating renewable portfolio 261.21 MW; 231.10 MW under construction, with land mostly acquired and PPAs signed.
Pune/Talegaon truck assembly facility inaugurated; battery pack assembly facility in same complex due for commissioning next quarter.
Management does not plan new government solar tenders; existing solar assets (operating and under construction) under evaluation for monetisation.
Plan of about 100 additional swap stations over 18 months, implying 200-300 MW of solar capacity, partly via open access and state-level partners.
EIM Megaplex incorporated as step-down subsidiary to hold charging, renewable and battery-as-a-service assets; paid-up equity INR 400 crore.
demand_pricing: Average selling price of an electric heavy truck about INR 60 lakh; energy packages (battery as a service, 7-year contracts) range INR 14-33 lakh per vehicle per year.
Customer savings of 5-20% on cost per ton-km; payback about 2.5 years, with INR 25 lakh upfront premium over diesel truck and INR 10 lakh annual saving with battery package.
MOUs with large transporters for almost 1,500 vehicles, to be converted into sales over one to two years; order book not disclosed.
Over 10 banks lend to customers for trucks without batteries; green leasing firms and large NBFCs also funding.
Half of sales in Q2 are repeat orders from existing customers. Sales cycle from engagement to conversion about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current average selling price per electric heavy commercial vehicle and how will pricing evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Average price about INR 60 lakh; 95% of sales are trucks without battery, with battery offered as a service under energy packages of INR 14-33 lakh per year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and how much capacity is backed by customer commitments?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book not disclosed; H2 sales guided to be significantly stronger than H1, supported by MOUs for about 1,500 vehicles to be converted in phases.

qa_highlights.question: Dependence on imported components given China technology restrictions?
qa_highlights.answer: Most heavy EV OEMs carry significant import content; battery cells and some critical motor parts will be imported for medium to long term, while non-electric parts are sourced domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Renewable capacity addition target for the next two to five years and FY28 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No new government tenders; focus on captive projects for charging network. FY28 EPC revenue around INR 600 crore if 200 MW is added; generation revenue INR 141-150 crore for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and milestones for the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Scheme filed with exchanges; expected to go to SEBI by end of November, then about three to four months of review before NCLT; likely completion around September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What drives EIM breakeven and what is the contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Contribution margin about 6% (earlier about 8%) due to rupee weakness; breakeven depends on volume growth in vehicles and network utilisation, with an annual run-rate of 2,000 vehicles seen as positive.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT dropped to INR 20.7 crore in H1 from INR 46.6 crore as EIM losses remain large; EIM still loss-making with breakeven targeted only in the next financial year.
Customer conversion timing: sales cycle about six months, and H2 ramp depends on charging infrastructure build-out and plant commissioning.
Import dependence for battery cells and motor parts; rupee weakness raises costs.
Monetisation of operating solar assets is a stated priority but no firm transaction or timeline disclosed; merger completion subject to regulatory approvals.
Network utilisation below 30% per station; 40 charging stations by March 2027 needs to be delivered.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on EIM demand, EV adoption and H2 ramp, with specific operating targets. Cautious and non-numeric on EIM losses and profitability timing, and evasive on the order book and diluted equity post-merger.
key_quotes: We sold a 142 vehicles last quarter as compared to 58 in the first quarter.
What we've learned is that the sale, from the time of engagement to conversion into sales, the cycle is about six months.
We can't disclose the order book, but one can guide that the second half sales will be significantly stronger than the first half.
We are focused entirely on this sector.

growth.why: Management guides 500 MW operating renewable capacity by March 2027 (200-220 MW added in FY27) and FY27 generation revenue of INR 141-150 crore vs INR 89 crore, with EPC revenue ~INR 600 crore (INR 200 crore booked in H1); the capacity build is under construction with land mostly acquired and PPAs signed, but EIM ramp relies on unquantified MOUs (~1,500 vehicles) and no disclosed order book.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Renewable EBITDA rose to INR 53 crore in Q2 from INR 33.4 crore, but EIM contribution margin fell to about 6% from about 8% on rupee weakness, and management gave no numeric EIM margin or loss guidance beyond narrowing losses in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Renewable capacity is 261.21 MW operating with 231.10 MW under construction, targeting about 300 MW by Q3 and 500 MW by March 2027 (200-220 MW added in FY27), and the Pune truck plant is already commissioned with regular production of about 200 units a month from January 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: EIM sales rose to 142 vehicles in Q2 from 58 in Q1 and management guides H2 significantly stronger than H1, supported by MOUs for about 1,500 vehicles, though the order book is not disclosed and conversion takes about six months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Plan of about 100 additional swap stations over 18 months implying 200-300 MW of solar is stated, but no firm capex amount or board approval is disclosed and management says no new government solar tenders.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as new in this call (500 MW by March 2027, FY27 generation revenue INR 141-150 crore) with no record of beating it, and EIM still loss-making with consolidated PAT of INR 20.7 crore in H1 versus INR 46.6 crore a year earlier.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 40-station charging target by March 2027 requires a build from 8 stations today, utilisation is below 30% per station, and the 200-220 MW addition depends on construction that is 231.10 MW under way; a slip would hit EPC and generation revenue guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Battery pack assembly facility at Talegaon is due for commissioning next quarter, with a CATL battery pack assembly tie-up announced, and battery-as-a-service energy packages are already offered at INR 14-33 lakh per vehicle per year.

rows.label: EIM Megaplex merger completion
rows.why: Scheme filed with exchanges, to go to SEBI by end-November and then about three to four months of NCLT review, with completion targeted around September 2027 and the company's paid-up equity in EIM Megaplex at INR 400 crore; management was evasive on diluted equity post-merger.

rows.label: EIM breakeven / positive
rows.why: Management targets EIM turning positive in the next financial year, with a run-rate of 2,000 vehicles a year seen as positive, but Q2 contribution margin fell to about 6% from about 8% and no numeric guidance was given.

rows.label: Solar asset monetisation
rows.why: Operating and under-construction solar assets are under evaluation for monetisation as a stated priority, but no firm transaction or timeline has been disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the renewable build-out (500 MW by March 2027), EIM H2 ramp and EV adoption, but cautious and non-numeric on EIM losses and breakeven timing and evasive on the order book and post-merger diluted equity; the brief does not record specific analyst pushback beyond the import
